name: The slow fan in Class XI-B
subject: repair
brief: The ceiling fan in Class XI-B turns, but slowly, even on its top setting. Ms Basu will not have the room closed, so you may test only in the break, and the school owns a single tachometer that the caretaker lends out one reading at a time. There are four things it could be, and the break is not long enough to test them all.

causes.name: Dust has caked the blade edges
The regulator is stuck on a low step

tests.name: Spin the blades by hand with the power off
Look along the blade edges for caked dust
Listen for a hum at switch-on before the blades pick up
Read the speed at every regulator step with a tachometer
Fit a known-good capacitor and run the fan

note: Class XI classrooms are from INDIA_WORLD_BIBLE.md (loc_nhss). Equipment is the scarce resource: every tachometer reading costs a unit more. A hum separates {capacitor, regulator} from the rest in one cheap look; the swap isolates the capacitor outright but costs most.
